paragraphs.text: Young Fashion Designer UK is an exciting national competition which aims to showcase and promote the exceptional work achieved by students studying courses in textile design, product design and fashion throughout the UK.
paragraphs.translation: 英国青年时装设计师大赛是一项激动人心的全国性竞赛，旨在展示和推广在英国各地学习纺织品设计、产品设计和时装课程的学生所取得的杰出作品。

paragraphs.text: The competition is designed for students to enter the coursework they are currently working on rather than specifically producing different pieces of work. If you would like to add to your coursework, that is for you and your teacher to decide.
paragraphs.translation:
该比赛旨在让学生提交他们目前正在进行的课程作业，而不是专门制作不同的作品。
如果您想对课程作业进行补充，这由您和您的老师自行决定。

paragraphs.text: You can apply independently or through your school/college. To enter please ensure you follow these steps:
paragraphs.translation:
你可以独立申请，或者通过你的学校/学院申请。
若要参赛，请确保遵循以下步骤：

paragraphs.text: 1) Provide three A3 colour copies from your design folder.
paragraphs.translation: 1) 从你的设计文件夹中提供三份A3彩色复印件。

paragraphs.text: You must include:
paragraphs.translation: 你必须包含：

paragraphs.text: - initial ideas about the clothing
paragraphs.translation: - 关于服装的初步构思

paragraphs.text: - a close-up photograph of the front and back view of the finished clothing.
paragraphs.translation: - 成品服装正面和背面视角的特写照片。

paragraphs.text: 2) Please label each sheet clearly with your name and school (on the back).
paragraphs.translation: 2) 请在每个页面的背面清晰标注你的姓名和学校。

paragraphs.text: 3) Print off a copy of your registration form and attach it to your work.
paragraphs.translation: 3) 打印一份你的注册表格副本，并将其附在你的作品上。

paragraphs.text: 4) Post your entry to the Young Fashion Designer Centre.
paragraphs.translation: 4) 将参赛作品邮寄至青年时装设计师中心。

paragraphs.text: Once the entry deadline has passed, the judges will select the shortlist of students who will be invited to the Finals. You will be notified if you are shortlisted. You will need to bring originals of the work that you entered. Each finalist will have their own stand consisting of a table and tabletop cardboard display panels. Feel free to add as much creativity to your stand as possible. Some students bring tablets/laptops with slideshows or further images of work but it should be emphasised that these may not necessarily improve your chances of success.
paragraphs.translation:
一旦参赛截止日期过去，评委将选出受邀参加决赛的入围学生名单。
如果你被列入候选名单，你会收到通知。
你需要带上你提交作品的原始件。
每位决赛选手将拥有自己的展位，包括一张桌子和桌面纸板展示板。
请尽情为你的展位增添尽可能多的创意。
一些学生会带平板电脑或笔记本电脑来播放幻灯片或展示更多作品图片，但需要强调的是，这些不一定能提高你成功的机会。

paragraphs.text: The judges will assess your work and will ask various questions about it. They will look through any supporting information and the work you have on display before coming together as a judging panel to decide on the winners. You are welcome to ask the judges questions. In fact, you should make the most of having experts on hand!
paragraphs.translation:
评委将评估你的作品，并会就其提出各种问题。
他们会在组成评审团共同决定获奖者之前，仔细查看任何辅助信息以及你展示的作品。
欢迎你向评委提问。
事实上，你应该充分利用有专家在场的机会！

paragraphs.text: There are 1st, 2nd and 3rd prize winners for each category. The judges can also decide to award special prizes if the work merits this. The 1st, 2nd and 3rd place winners will receive a glass trophy and prize from a kind donor.
paragraphs.translation:
每个类别都有一、二、三等奖的获奖者。
如果作品值得，评委也可以决定颁发特别奖。
一、二、三等奖的获奖者将获得一座玻璃奖杯和来自一位慷慨捐赠者的奖品。

paragraphs.text: Which keyboard should you buy?
paragraphs.translation: 你应该购买哪款键盘？

paragraphs.text: It's worth remembering that a bad keyboard can significantly affect your entire computing experience. So make sure you pick the right keyboard for your needs.
paragraphs.translation:
值得记住的是，一个糟糕的键盘可能会显著影响你的整体计算体验。
因此，确保你根据自身需求选择合适的键盘。

paragraphs.text: A Logitech K120
paragraphs.translation: 一款罗技K120键盘

paragraphs.text: Logitech's K120 offers a number of extra features. It's spill-resistant, draining small amounts of liquid if you have an accident. It isn't particularly eye-catching, but it feels very solid. For the price, it's a tempting choice.
paragraphs.translation:
罗技K120提供了许多额外功能。
它具有防泼溅特性，如果不小心洒上少量液体，可以将其排出。
它并非特别引人注目，但手感非常扎实。
就其价格而言，这是一个诱人的选择。

paragraphs.text: B Cherry MX 3.0 Keyboard
paragraphs.translation: B 樱桃MX 3.0键盘

paragraphs.text: The Cherry MX 3.0 looks simple and neat, thanks to its compact build. It's solid, durable and you don't need to push keys all the way down to activate them. It's also rather loud though, which can take some getting used to.
paragraphs.translation:
Cherry MX 3.0键盘因其紧凑的设计而显得简洁利落。
它坚固耐用，而且你无需将按键完全按下即可触发。
然而，它的声音也相当响亮，这可能需要一些时间来适应。

paragraphs.text: C Logitech K780
paragraphs.translation: C 罗技 K780

paragraphs.text: The K780 is a compact, pleasantly modern-looking keyboard. There's an integrated stand for smartphones and tablets too. It's quiet to type on, and the circular keys are easy to familiarise yourself with, well-spaced and large enough to hit accurately. For this price though, the lack of backlighting is disappointing.
paragraphs.translation:
K780是一款紧凑且外观现代宜人的键盘。
它还配有一个集成的支架，用于放置智能手机和平板电脑。
打字时很安静，圆形按键易于熟悉，间距合理且足够大，便于准确敲击。
不过，就这个价格而言，缺少背光功能令人失望。

paragraphs.text: D Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic
paragraphs.translation: D 微软 Sculpt 人体工学键盘

paragraphs.text: The Sculpt's curved, strange-looking build serves a purpose. It provides wrist support and lifts your forearms into a relaxed position so you don't hurt yourself from typing for lengthy periods. It feels weird, but it seems to do the trick.
paragraphs.translation:
Sculpt键盘的弯曲、外形奇特的构造是有其用途的。
它提供手腕支撑，并将前臂抬高至放松的位置，这样你就不会因长时间打字而受伤。
感觉有些奇怪，但似乎能起到作用。

paragraphs.text: E Microsoft Universal Bluetooth Keyboard
paragraphs.translation: E 微软通用蓝牙键盘

paragraphs.text: Microsoft's Bluetooth keyboard has one very handy feature - you can fold it in half and carry it around in your jacket pocket or bag, and it feels rather like a large wallet. It has generously sized keys, though the two-piece space bar takes some getting used to. Another useful feature is that you can get up to three months' use from a single charge.
paragraphs.translation:
微软的蓝牙键盘有一个非常便捷的功能——你可以将它对折，放在夹克口袋或包里携带，感觉就像一个大钱包。
它的按键尺寸宽大，不过分体式的空格键需要一些时间来适应。
另一个有用的功能是，单次充电后可以使用长达三个月。

paragraphs.text: F Corsair Strafe RGB Keyboard
paragraphs.translation: F 海盗船惩戒者 RGB 键盘

paragraphs.text: Corsair's keyboard is expensive, flashy and extremely impressive. All of its keys are programmable, there's eye-catching backlighting and the buttons are textured for improved grip. All this is because it's designed for gamers. However, it's also silent, meaning it is suitable for everyday office work too.
paragraphs.translation:
海盗船的键盘价格昂贵、炫目且极为出色。
其所有按键均可编程，拥有引人注目的背光，且按键带有纹理以增强抓握感。
这一切都是因为它专为游戏玩家设计。
不过，它也很安静，这意味着它也适用于日常办公。

paragraphs.text: A

Recent research shows that many job-seekers believe their ideal position would be in a large company. However, working for a small or medium-sized business has many advantages that are too easily overlooked. Here are just a few of them.
paragraphs.translation:
最近的研究表明，许多求职者认为他们理想的职位会在一个大公司。
然而，在中小型企业工作有许多容易被忽视的优势。
以下只是其中的一些。

paragraphs.text: B

Working in a small organisation with a small workforce means it's likely to be easy to become part of it. It won't be long before you're familiar with the staff and the departments that you need to deal with. This can provide a feeling of comfort that takes much longer to develop in a large company. Departments are likely to be small and have close connections with each other, which helps to make internal communication work well -everyone knows what's going on. You'll also gain a better understanding of how your own role fits into the company as a whole.
paragraphs.translation:
在员工人数较少的小型组织工作意味着你很容易融入其中。
不久之后，你就会熟悉需要打交道的同事和部门。
这能带来一种舒适感，而在大公司里，这种感受需要更长时间才能培养起来。
部门可能规模较小且彼此联系紧密，这有助于内部沟通顺畅进行——每个人都知道正在发生什么。
你还将更好地理解自己的角色如何融入整个公司。
在员工人数较少的小型组织中工作，意味着你很容易融入其中。
不用多久，你就会熟悉需要打交道的同事和部门。
这能带来一种舒适感，而在大公司里，这种舒适感需要更长的时间才能培养起来。
部门通常规模较小且相互之间联系紧密，这有助于内部沟通顺畅进行——每个人都知道正在发生什么。
你还会更清楚地理解自己的角色如何融入整个公司。

paragraphs.text: C

In a small business you're likely to have considerable variety in your workload, including opportunities to work in different areas of the company, which will allow you to identify abilities that you didn't know you had. An introduction to new activities could even lead to a change of career. This variety in your work will help to make it stimulating, so you have a good reason for getting out of bed in the morning.
paragraphs.translation:
在小公司里，你的工作量很可能会相当多样化，包括有机会在公司不同领域工作，这将使你能够发现自己以前不知道的能力。
接触新活动甚至可能带来职业上的转变。
工作中的这种多样性将使其充满激励性，从而让你有充分的理由每天早晨起床。

paragraphs.text: D

There will be plenty of opportunities to show initiative, and you'll also learn to function well as part of a team. Because it's much harder to overlook someone within a small workforce than a large one, your efforts are more likely to attract the attention of those higher up. You'll have plenty of opportunity to show what you can do, and to have your potential noticed. The result is very likely to be that promotion comes to you faster.
paragraphs.translation:
将会有大量机会展示主动性，同时你也会学会如何在团队中高效协作。
因为在小型团队中忽视某个人远比在大公司中困难得多，你的努力更有可能引起上级的注意。
你将有充足的机会展示自己的能力，并让你的潜力得到关注。
结果很可能是你会更快获得晋升机会。
你将会有很多机会展现主动性，同时还能学会如何在团队中高效运作。
因为在小型团队中忽视某人比在大型组织中难得多，你的努力更容易引起上级的注意。
你将有充足的机会展示自己的能力，并让自身的潜力得到关注。
结果很可能是晋升会更快地降临到你身上。

paragraphs.text: E

Small businesses are usually flexible, something that is rarely true of large organisations. This means that if they're well managed, they can adapt to make the most of changes in the wider economy, which in turn can help you. Don't dismiss them as a place to work because of the myths about them. Small firms can be ideal places for developing your career.
paragraphs.translation:
小型企业通常非常灵活，而这一点在大型组织中则很少见。
这意味着如果管理得当，它们能够适应并充分利用更广泛经济环境中的变化，而这反过来也能帮助你。
不要因为关于它们的种种传言而将它们视为不值得工作的场所。
小型公司可能是发展你职业生涯的理想之地。

paragraphs.text: Starting a new job
paragraphs.translation: 开始一份新工作

paragraphs.text: A

Make sure you know when and where you are expected to report on your first day. If the route from home is unfamiliar to you, make a practice run first: the normal first activity in a new job is a meeting with your boss, and it would be embarrassing to be late. Dress formally until you're sure of the dress code.
paragraphs.translation:
确保你清楚自己第一天上班应在何时何地报到。
如果从家出发的路线你不熟悉，先进行一次预演：新工作的第一个常规活动通常是和老板会面，迟到会很尴尬。
在确定着装要求之前，穿着正式服装。

paragraphs.text: B

You should expect to have an induction programme planned for you: a security pass; visits to whatever parts of the organisation you need to understand to do your job properly; meetings with anyone who could affect your success in the role; and someone to show you where everything is and tell you all the real rules of the culture - the ones that are never written down but which everyone is meant to follow.
paragraphs.translation:
你应该期望有一个为你规划好的入职培训计划：一张安全通行证；参观你需要了解的任何部门，以便正确完成工作；与任何可能影响你在这个职位上取得成功的人会面；以及有人带你熟悉一切位置，并告诉你所有真正的文化规则——那些从未写下来但每个人都应该遵守的规则。
你应该期待得到一个为你规划的入职培训计划：包括一张安全通行证；参观你需要了解以顺利开展工作的所有部门；与可能影响你职位成功的任何人会面；以及有人带你熟悉各处位置并告诉你所有真正的文化规则——那些从未写下但每个人都应遵守的规则。

paragraphs.text: C

It can be a shock to join a new organisation. When you are a newcomer, feeling uncertain and perhaps a little confused, there can be a strong temptation to talk about your old job and organisation as a way of reminding yourself and telling others that you really know what you are doing, because you did it in your previous role. Unfortunately, this will suggest that you have a high opinion of yourself, and that you think your old place was better. It has enormous power to annoy, so don't do it.
paragraphs.translation:
加入一个新组织可能会带来冲击。
作为一个新人，你会感到不确定，甚至有些困惑，这时可能有一种强烈的冲动去谈论你以前的工作和组织，以此提醒自己并告诉别人你确实知道自己在做什么，因为你以前做过这个职位。
不幸的是，这会让别人觉得你自视甚高，并认为你以前的工作单位更好。
这很容易令人反感，所以不要这样做。
加入一个新机构可能会让人感到震惊。
当你是一名新员工，感到不确定、甚至有些困惑时，很容易产生强烈的冲动，想要谈论自己以前的工作和机构，以此提醒自己并告诉别人你确实知道自己在做什么，因为你在之前的职位上做过这些。
不幸的是，这会让人觉得你自我评价过高，并且认为你之前的工作地方更好。
这种行为极易惹恼他人，所以千万不要这样做。

paragraphs.text: D

All employers have a core product or service paid for by customers which justifies their existence. If you are not part of this core activity, remember that your role is to provide a service to the people who are part of it. Understanding their concerns and passions is essential for understanding why your own role exists, and for knowing how to work alongside these colleagues. This is why you must see this product or service in action.
paragraphs.translation:
所有雇主都有一个由客户付费的核心产品或服务，这证明了它们存在的合理性。
如果你不属于这一核心活动的一部分，请记住你的职责是为参与其中的人提供服务。
理解他们的顾虑和热情对于领悟自身职位存在的原因以及学会如何与这些同事共事至关重要。
这就是为什么你必须亲眼见证这一产品或服务的实际运作。

paragraphs.text: E

When I worked for a television company, all of us, whatever our job, were strongly encouraged to visit a studio and see how programmes were made. This was wise. Make sure you do the equivalent for whatever is the core activity of your new employer.
paragraphs.translation:
当我在一家电视公司工作时，我们所有人，无论职位如何，都被大力鼓励去参观演播室，看看节目是如何制作的。
这是明智之举。
确保你针对新雇主的任何核心活动都做同样的事情。
当我曾在一家电视公司工作时，无论我们担任什么职位，都被强烈鼓励参观演播室，了解节目是如何制作的。

paragraphs.text: F

Don't try to do the job too soon. This may seem strange because, after all, you have been appointed to get on and do the job. But in your first few weeks your task is to learn what the job really is, rather than immediately starting to do what you assume it is.
paragraphs.translation:
不要急于立刻投入工作。
这也许看起来很奇怪，因为毕竟你是被指派来着手完成这份工作的。
但在最初的几周里，你的任务是了解这份工作的真实内容，而不是立即开始做你自认为的工作。
不要过早尝试执行工作任务。
这看起来可能有些奇怪，因为毕竟你被任命是为了接手并完成这份工作。
但在最初的几周内，你的任务是了解这份工作的实质内容，而不是立即开始做你自认为的工作。

paragraphs.text: G

Starting a new job is one of life's major transitions. Treat it with the attention it deserves and you will find that all your work in preparing and then going through the selection process has paid off magnificently.
paragraphs.translation:
开始一份新工作
开始一份新工作是人生中重大的转折点之一。
以应有的重视来对待它，你会发现之前在准备并经历选拔过程中付出的所有努力都得到了极为丰厚的回报。
开始一份新工作是人生中重要的转变之一。
以应有的重视对待它，你会发现你在准备和经历选拔过程中的所有努力都得到了丰厚的回报。

Halsey points out that this may not necessarily be the case. Take the house cat. Most domestic cats spend much of the day lounging around, apparently doing nothing, rather than hunting for food. 但在短距离内，即使是最懒的猫也能在想要时移动得极快。
同样，黑熊和棕熊在长达数月的冬眠后，肌肉量仍能保持完好——在这段时间内它们甚至无需抬一下爪子。

paragraphs.text: E

Barnacle geese go one better. In the process of sitting around, they don't just maintain their fitness. They also develop stronger hearts and bigger flight muscles, enabling them to fly for thousands of kilometres in a migration that may last as little as two days.
paragraphs.translation:
藤壶鹅更胜一筹。
在无所事事的过程中，它们不仅维持了健康。
它们还发展出更强壮的心脏和更大的飞行肌肉，使其能在可能仅持续两天的迁徙中飞行数千公里。

paragraphs.text: F

So, if exercise isn't necessarily the key to physical strength, then what is? One clue comes from a broader view of the meaning of physical fitness. Biologically speaking, all it means is that the body has undergone changes that make it stronger and more efficient. In animals such as bears these changes appear to be triggered by cues such as falling temperatures or insufficient food. In the months of hibernation, these factors seem to prompt the release of muscle-protecting compounds which are then carried to the bears' muscles in their blood and prevent muscle loss.
paragraphs.translation:
那么，如果锻炼不一定是体力的关键，那什么才是呢？
一个线索来自于对身体素质含义的更广泛理解。
从生物学角度来说，这仅仅意味着身体经历了变化，使其更强壮、更高效。
在像熊这样的动物中，这些变化似乎是由气温下降或食物不足等信号触发的。
在几个月的冬眠期间，这些因素似乎促使肌肉保护化合物的释放，随后通过血液输送到熊的肌肉中，从而防止肌肉流失。

paragraphs.text: G

Barnacle geese, Halsey suggests, may be responding to an environmental change such as temperature, which helps their bodies somehow ' know' that a big physical challenge is looming. In other bird species, that cue may be something different. Chris Guglielmo, a physiological ecologist, has studied the effect of subjecting migratory songbirds known as yellow-rumped warblers to changing hours of daylight."We don' t need to take little songbirds and train them up to do a 6- or 10-hour flight,' he says. If they are subjected to the right daylight cycle,'we can take them out of the cage and put them in the wind tunnel, and they fly for 10 hours.'
paragraphs.translation:
哈西认为，白颊黑雁可能正在对诸如温度之类的环境变化做出反应，这以某种方式帮助它们的身体‘知道’一个巨大的体能挑战即将来临。
在其他鸟类物种中，这种信号可能有所不同。
生理生态学家克里斯·古列尔莫研究了让被称为黄腰林莺的迁徙鸣禽接受日照时长变化的效应。
“我们不需要带着小鸣禽并训练它们进行6或10小时的飞行，”他说。
如果让它们处于合适的日照周期中，“我们可以把它们从笼子里拿出来放进风洞，它们就会飞行10个小时。”

paragraphs.text: H
Unlike migratory birds, however, humans have no biological shortcut to getting fit. Instead, pressures in our evolutionary history made our bodies tie fitness to exercise.
paragraphs.translation:
然而，与候鸟不同，人类没有获得健康的生物学捷径。
相反，我们进化历史中的压力使身体将健康与锻炼紧密联系在一起。
然而，与候鸟不同，人类没有生物上的捷径来保持健康。
相反，我们进化历史中的压力使身体将健康与锻炼联系在一起。

paragraphs.text: I

Our ancestors' lives were unpredictable. They had to do a lot of running to catch food and escape danger, but they also needed to keep muscle mass to a minimum because muscle is biologically expensive. Each kilogram contributes about 10 to 15 kilocalories a day to our metabolism when resting - which doesn't sound like much until you realise that muscles account for about 40 percent of the average person's body mass. 'Most of us are spending 20 percent of our basic energy budget taking care of muscle mass, says Daniel Lieberman, an evolutionary biologist and marathon runner.
paragraphs.translation:
我们祖先的生活是难以预测的。
他们不得不进行大量奔跑以捕食和躲避危险，但也需要将肌肉量保持在最低限度，因为肌肉在生物学上代价高昂。
每公斤肌肉在休息时每天会为我们的新陈代谢贡献约10到15千卡热量——这听起来并不多，直到你意识到肌肉约占普通人身体质量的40%。
“我们大多数人将基础能量预算的20%用于维持肌肉量，”进化生物学家兼马拉松跑者丹尼尔·利伯曼说道。

paragraphs.text: J

So our physiology evolved to let our weight and fitness fluctuate depending on how much food was available."This makes us evolutionarily different from most other animals，'says Lieberman. In general, animals merely need to be capable of short bouts of intense activity, whether it's the cheetah chasing prey or the gazelle escaping. Cats are fast, but they don’t need to run very far. Perhaps a few mad dashes around the house are all it takes to keep a domestic one fit enough for feline purposes. 'Humans, on the other hand, needed to adapt to run slower, but for longer,' says Lieberman.
paragraphs.translation:
因此，我们的生理机能进化使得体重和健康状况根据食物获取量的多少而波动。
“这使得我们在进化上不同于大多数其他动物，”利伯曼说。
总的来说，动物只需具备进行短暂剧烈活动的能力，无论是猎豹追捕猎物还是瞪羚逃跑都是如此。
猫跑得很快，但它们不需要跑很远。
也许在屋内几次疯狂冲刺就足以让家猫保持足以满足猫科动物需求的健康状态。
“另一方面，人类需要适应跑得更慢但更久，”利伯曼说。

paragraphs.text: K

He argues that long ago on the African savannah, natural selection made us into ‘supremely adapted' endurance athletes, capable of running prey into the ground and ranging over long distances with unusual efficiency. But only, it appears, if we train. Otherwise we quickly degenerate into couch potatoes.
paragraphs.translation:
他认为，在很久以前的非洲大草原上，自然选择使我们成为‘高度适应’的耐力运动员，能够将猎物追至筋疲力尽，并以异常高效的方式长途跋涉。
但似乎，只有当我们训练时才能如此。
否则，我们会迅速退化为懒散的沙发土豆。

paragraphs.text: L

As for speed, even those animals that do cover impressive distances don’t have to be the fastest they can possibly be. Barnacle geese needn’t set world records when crossing the North Atlantic; they just need to be able to get to their destination. 'And,'says exercise physiologist Ross Tucker,'humans may be the only animal that actually cares about reaching peak performance.' Other than racehorses and greyhounds, both of which we have bred to race, animals aren't directly competing against one another. 'I don't know that all animals are the same, performance-wise... and we don’t know whether training would enhance their ability，'he says.
paragraphs.translation:
至于速度，即使是那些能够跨越惊人距离的动物，也不必非要达到它们可能达到的最快速度。
白颊黑雁在飞越北大西洋时无需创造世界纪录；它们只需要能够抵达目的地。
运动生理学家罗斯·塔克说：‘而且，人类可能是唯一真正在意达到巅峰表现的动物。’
除了我们培育用于赛跑的马和灵缇犬之外，动物们并不直接相互竞争。
他说：‘我不知道所有动物在表现能力方面是否相同……我们也不知道训练是否会提升它们的能力。’
至于速度，即使是那些行进了惊人距离的动物，也不必达到它们可能的最快速度。
白颊黑雁在飞越北大西洋时不必创造世界纪录；它们只需要能够到达目的地。
运动生理学家罗斯·塔克说：“而且，人类可能是唯一真正在意达到最佳表现的动物。”
除了我们培育来比赛的马和灵缇犬之外，动物们并不直接相互竞争。
他说：“我不知道所有动物在表现方面是否都一样……我们也不知道训练是否会提高它们的能力。”

sentence_translations.sentence: Instead, says environmental physiologist Lewis Halsey, "They just basically sit on the water and eat a lot."

sentence_translations.sentence: Now consider the barnacle goose.
sentence_translations.translation: 现在考虑一下白颊黑雁。

sentence_translations.sentence: Every year this bird carries out a 3000-kilometre migration.
sentence_translations.translation: 每年，这种鸟都会进行一次长达3000公里的迁徙。

sentence_translations.sentence: So how do the birds prepare for this?
sentence_translations.translation: 那么，这些鸟是如何为此做准备的？

sentence_translations.sentence: Do they spend months gradually building up fitness?
sentence_translations.translation: 它们是否会花费数月时间逐渐增强体能？

sentence_translations.sentence: That's not really the barnacle goose's style.
sentence_translations.translation: 这并非白颊黑雁的风格。

sentence_translations.sentence: Instead, says environmental physiologist Lewis Halsey, "They just basically sit on the water and eat a lot.'
sentence_translations.translation: 相反，环境生理学家刘易斯·哈尔西说：“它们基本上只是待在水面上，大量进食。”

sentence_translations.sentence: Until recently, nobody had really asked whether exercise is as tightly connected to fitness in the rest of the animal kingdom as it is for us.
sentence_translations.translation: 直到最近，还没有人真正探究过：在动物界中，运动是否与我们人类一样，与体质健康紧密相连。

sentence_translations.sentence: The question is tied up in a broader assumption: that animals maintain fitness because of the exercise they get finding food and escaping predators.
sentence_translations.translation: 这个问题涉及一个更广泛的假设：动物之所以能保持健康体质，是因为它们在觅食和躲避捕食者的过程中得到了锻炼。

sentence_translations.sentence: Halsey points out that this may not necessarily be the case.
sentence_translations.translation: 哈尔西指出，这未必是事实。

sentence_translations.sentence: Take the house cat.
sentence_translations.translation: 以家猫为例。

sentence_translations.sentence: Most domestic cats spend much of the day lounging around, apparently doing nothing, rather than hunting for food.
sentence_translations.translation: 大多数家猫一天中大部分时间都在闲逛，显然无所事事，而不是捕猎食物。

sentence_translations.sentence: But over short distances, even the laziest can move incredibly fast when they want to.
sentence_translations.translation: 但在短距离内，即使是最懒的猫也能在想要时移动得极快。

sentence_translations.sentence: Similarly, black and brown bears manage to come out of several months' hibernation with their muscle mass intact - without having to lift so much as a paw during this time.
sentence_translations.translation: 同样，黑熊和棕熊在长达数月的冬眠后，肌肉量仍能保持完好——在这段时间内它们甚至无需抬一下爪子。

sentence_translations.sentence: Barnacle geese go one better.
sentence_translations.translation: 藤壶鹅更胜一筹。

sentence_translations.sentence: In the process of sitting around, they don't just maintain their fitness.
sentence_translations.translation: 在无所事事的过程中，它们不仅维持了健康。

sentence_translations.sentence: They also develop stronger hearts and bigger flight muscles, enabling them to fly for thousands of kilometres in a migration that may last as little as two days.
sentence_translations.translation: 它们还发展出更强壮的心脏和更大的飞行肌肉，使其能在可能仅持续两天的迁徙中飞行数千公里。

sentence_translations.sentence: So, if exercise isn't necessarily the key to physical strength, then what is?
sentence_translations.translation: 那么，如果锻炼不一定是体力的关键，那什么才是呢？

sentence_translations.sentence: One clue comes from a broader view of the meaning of physical fitness.
sentence_translations.translation: 一个线索来自于对身体素质含义的更广泛理解。

sentence_translations.sentence: Biologically speaking, all it means is that the body has undergone changes that make it stronger and more efficient.
sentence_translations.translation: 从生物学角度来说，这仅仅意味着身体经历了变化，使其更强壮、更高效。

sentence_translations.sentence: In animals such as bears these changes appear to be triggered by cues such as falling temperatures or insufficient food.
sentence_translations.translation: 在像熊这样的动物中，这些变化似乎是由气温下降或食物不足等信号触发的。

sentence_translations.sentence: In the months of hibernation, these factors seem to prompt the release of muscle-protecting compounds which are then carried to the bears' muscles in their blood and prevent muscle loss.
sentence_translations.translation: 在几个月的冬眠期间，这些因素似乎促使肌肉保护化合物的释放，随后通过血液输送到熊的肌肉中，从而防止肌肉流失。

sentence_translations.sentence: Barnacle geese, Halsey suggests, may be responding to an environmental change such as temperature, which helps their bodies somehow ' know' that a big physical challenge is looming.
sentence_translations.translation: 哈西认为，白颊黑雁可能正在对诸如温度之类的环境变化做出反应，这以某种方式帮助它们的身体‘知道’一个巨大的体能挑战即将来临。

sentence_translations.sentence: In other bird species, that cue may be something different.
sentence_translations.translation: 在其他鸟类物种中，这种信号可能有所不同。

sentence_translations.sentence: Chris Guglielmo, a physiological ecologist, has studied the effect of subjecting migratory songbirds known as yellow-rumped warblers to changing hours of daylight.
sentence_translations.translation: 生理生态学家克里斯·古列尔莫研究了让被称为黄腰林莺的迁徙鸣禽接受日照时长变化的效应。

sentence_translations.sentence: "We don' t need to take little songbirds and train them up to do a 6- or 10-hour flight,' he says.
sentence_translations.translation: “我们不需要带着小鸣禽并训练它们进行6或10小时的飞行，”他说。

sentence_translations.sentence: If they are subjected to the right daylight cycle,'we can take them out of the cage and put them in the wind tunnel, and they fly for 10 hours.'
sentence_translations.translation: 如果让它们处于合适的日照周期中，“我们可以把它们从笼子里拿出来放进风洞，它们就会飞行10个小时。”

sentence_translations.sentence: Unlike migratory birds, however, humans have no biological shortcut to getting fit.
sentence_translations.translation: 然而，与候鸟不同，人类没有获得健康的生物学捷径。

sentence_translations.sentence: Instead, pressures in our evolutionary history made our bodies tie fitness to exercise.
sentence_translations.translation: 相反，我们进化历史中的压力使身体将健康与锻炼紧密联系在一起。

sentence_translations.sentence: Unlike migratory birds, however, humans have no biological shortcut to getting fit.
sentence_translations.translation: 然而，与候鸟不同，人类没有生物上的捷径来保持健康。

sentence_translations.sentence: Instead, pressures in our evolutionary history made our bodies tie fitness to exercise.
sentence_translations.translation: 相反，我们进化历史中的压力使身体将健康与锻炼联系在一起。

sentence_translations.sentence: Our ancestors' lives were unpredictable.
sentence_translations.translation: 我们祖先的生活是难以预测的。

sentence_translations.sentence: They had to do a lot of running to catch food and escape danger, but they also needed to keep muscle mass to a minimum because muscle is biologically expensive.
sentence_translations.translation: 他们不得不进行大量奔跑以捕食和躲避危险，但也需要将肌肉量保持在最低限度，因为肌肉在生物学上代价高昂。

sentence_translations.sentence: Each kilogram contributes about 10 to 15 kilocalories a day to our metabolism when resting - which doesn't sound like much until you realise that muscles account for about 40 percent of the average person's body mass.
sentence_translations.translation: 每公斤肌肉在休息时每天会为我们的新陈代谢贡献约10到15千卡热量——这听起来并不多，直到你意识到肌肉约占普通人身体质量的40%。

sentence_translations.sentence: 'Most of us are spending 20 percent of our basic energy budget taking care of muscle mass, says Daniel Lieberman, an evolutionary biologist and marathon runner.
sentence_translations.translation: “我们大多数人将基础能量预算的20%用于维持肌肉量，”进化生物学家兼马拉松跑者丹尼尔·利伯曼说道。

sentence_translations.sentence: So our physiology evolved to let our weight and fitness fluctuate depending on how much food was available.
sentence_translations.translation: 因此，我们的生理机能进化使得体重和健康状况根据食物获取量的多少而波动。

sentence_translations.sentence: "This makes us evolutionarily different from most other animals，"says Lieberman.
sentence_translations.translation: “这使得我们在进化上不同于大多数其他动物，”利伯曼说。

sentence_translations.sentence: In general, animals merely need to be capable of short bouts of intense activity, whether it's the cheetah chasing prey or the gazelle escaping.
sentence_translations.translation: 总的来说，动物只需具备进行短暂剧烈活动的能力，无论是猎豹追捕猎物还是瞪羚逃跑都是如此。

sentence_translations.sentence: Cats are fast, but they don’t need to run very far.
sentence_translations.translation: 猫跑得很快，但它们不需要跑很远。

sentence_translations.sentence: Perhaps a few mad dashes around the house are all it takes to keep a domestic one fit enough for feline purposes.
sentence_translations.translation: 也许在屋内几次疯狂冲刺就足以让家猫保持足以满足猫科动物需求的健康状态。

sentence_translations.sentence: 'Humans, on the other hand, needed to adapt to run slower, but for longer,' says Lieberman.
sentence_translations.translation: “另一方面，人类需要适应跑得更慢但更久，”利伯曼说。

sentence_translations.sentence: He argues that long ago on the African savannah, natural selection made us into ‘supremely adapted' endurance athletes, capable of running prey into the ground and ranging over long distances with unusual efficiency.
sentence_translations.translation: 他认为，在很久以前的非洲大草原上，自然选择使我们成为‘高度适应’的耐力运动员，能够将猎物追至筋疲力尽，并以异常高效的方式长途跋涉。

sentence_translations.sentence: But only, it appears, if we train.
sentence_translations.translation: 但似乎，只有当我们训练时才能如此。

sentence_translations.sentence: Otherwise we quickly degenerate into couch potatoes.
sentence_translations.translation: 否则，我们会迅速退化为懒散的沙发土豆。

sentence_translations.sentence: As for speed, even those animals that do cover impressive distances don’t have to be the fastest they can possibly be.
sentence_translations.translation: 至于速度，即使是那些能够跨越惊人距离的动物，也不必非要达到它们可能达到的最快速度。

sentence_translations.sentence: Barnacle geese needn’t set world records when crossing the North Atlantic; they just need to be able to get to their destination.
sentence_translations.translation: 白颊黑雁在飞越北大西洋时无需创造世界纪录；它们只需要能够抵达目的地。

sentence_translations.sentence: 'And,'says exercise physiologist Ross Tucker,'humans may be the only animal that actually cares about reaching peak performance.'
sentence_translations.translation: 运动生理学家罗斯·塔克说：‘而且，人类可能是唯一真正在意达到巅峰表现的动物。’

sentence_translations.sentence: Other than racehorses and greyhounds, both of which we have bred to race, animals aren't directly competing against one another.
sentence_translations.translation: 除了我们培育用于赛跑的马和灵缇犬之外，动物们并不直接相互竞争。

sentence_translations.sentence: 'I don't know that all animals are the same, performance-wise... and we don’t know whether training would enhance their ability，'he says.
sentence_translations.translation: 他说：‘我不知道所有动物在表现能力方面是否相同……我们也不知道训练是否会提升它们的能力。’

sentence_translations.sentence: As for speed, even those animals that do cover impressive distances don’t have to be the fastest they can possibly be.
sentence_translations.translation: 至于速度，即使是那些行进了惊人距离的动物，也不必达到它们可能的最快速度。

sentence_translations.sentence: Other than racehorses and greyhounds, both of which we have bred to race, animals aren't directly competing against one another.
sentence_translations.translation: 除了我们培育来比赛的马和灵缇犬之外，动物们并不直接相互竞争。

sentence_translations.sentence: 'I don't know that all animals are the same, performance-wise... and we don’t know whether training would enhance their ability，'he says.
sentence_translations.translation: 他说：“我不知道所有动物在表现方面是否都一样……我们也不知道训练是否会提高它们的能力。”
